_role: describer_style ENRICHED ROUND -- only the images added in s15, scored against the master table in docs/image_inventory.md. NOT a representative sample of the corpus: collected to fill named gaps, so it is deliberately skewed and a failure RATE over it says nothing about the corpus as a whole.
_generated: Built by scripts/gen_style_sweep.py, which parses the master table, so the answer key cannot drift from the corpus. Groups are the expected coarse medium, which makes a miss visible in the run file itself. NOTE: these are NOT drift groups -- validate.py only cross-checks groups named 'same: ...', and none here are.
_hand_edited: NO LONGER SAFE TO REGENERATE. The generator's old instruction here said 'DO NOT HAND-EDIT -- regenerate'; that was correct until the round was adjudicated. As of s15 this file carries USER RULINGS that the master table does not encode, marked '(CONTESTED s15: ...)' in _expected. Re-running gen_style_sweep.py --added s15 would overwrite them with the plain master-table answer and silently re-accumulate settled cases against the thresholds. If you must regenerate, diff the new _expected against this one and carry every CONTESTED marker forward by hand. See L-DONT-REGENERATE-A-BASELINED-TEST for the same hazard in its other form.
_passes: TWO PASSES PER IMAGE (session 12). look_<name> runs prompts/describer_style_look.txt and emits the six descriptive fields; sw_<name> runs prompts/describer_style_class.txt, receives that record as its user prompt, and emits the four closed-vocabulary fields. The CLASSIFIER keeps the sw_ ids on purpose, so _expected is unchanged by the split. Validate each half separately: --role style_look --id-prefix look_ , then --role style_class --id-prefix sw_. NOTE this is now 2x the calls -- budget ~20 minutes.
_scoring: Four fields: MEDIUM / SUB_MEDIUM / IDIOM / TREATMENT, which is score.py's default, all emitted by the classifier pass; look_ records are not in _expected and are ignored by score.py. The session-9 instruction to treat drawing and painting sub-term misses as CONTESTED is RETIRED -- those sub-lists no longer mix axes, so score all four fields. Only the amb files stay excluded.
_accept_sets: Four cases carry accept-sets, ruled by the user in session 16: sw_avatar_1, sw_avatar_2, sw_boondocks, sw_titans1 -- the anime-idiom western cartoons. Each names strict CONTROLS on the same axis. score.py warns when an accept-set fires while a control COLLAPSES (drifts, on that axis, to a value the set forgives); a control missing for an unrelated reason is reported as "off-distinction" and raises nothing. Read that warning before crediting any of these with a pass.
_gate_note: Enriched, per .claude/CLAUDE.md: gate on MOVEMENT (regressions vs the previous round), never on the failure level. On the FIRST run there is no delta at all, so there is nothing to gate -- adjudicate, cap 6. Three of these images carry provisional rulings the user expects may need reversing; read docs/image_inventory.md section "Rulings that may need revisiting" BEFORE scoring them, or you will file a deliberate decision as a model defect.

sw_avatar_1.expect: 2D cel / digital / western toon | anime / colour
sw_avatar_1.why: a western toon with an anime-inspired style; the two traditions are genuinely converging (user, sessions 15 and 16). Written on ALL FOUR of the s15 anime-idiom cartoons, not only the two that failed this way in the s15 round -- the accept-set records a property of the IMAGE, and keying it to one run's output would be fitting the answer key to a sample (L-ONE-RUN-IS-A-SAMPLE). Score-neutral this round: boondocks missed to dimensional toon, outside the set, and titans1 passed on the primary. Controls guard both directions -- sw_april_1987 and sw_ivy_toon are unambiguously western, sw_nadia unambiguously anime. sw_ivy_toon lives in describer_style_sweep.json and will report 'not in this test' here; run the sweep to exercise it. EXPECT THE COLLAPSE WARNING: sw_april_1987 already answers `anime`, which is exactly what the control field exists to make visible -- it is not a reason to widen the set.
